title: gitapex agent metadata sidecar (AgentMetadata gitapex.io/v1alpha1)
description: Schema for every agents/metadata/<name>.gitapex.yaml sidecar (issue #2073, parent #307). Declares a subagent/agent type's own execution requirements, owned by the agent type rather than by whichever skill dispatches it. Same apiVersion/kind/metadata/spec envelope as skills/evaluating-skill-quality/references/skill-metadata.schema.json, with a distinct kind. Declaration only: no adapter consumes this yet, so nothing here is enforced at runtime. Cross-file rules this schema cannot express (metadata.name equals the file's <name> stem, agents/<name>.md exists, exitConditions[].id is unique) live in .github/scripts/gitapex_scan_agent_metadata_schema.py.

name.description: Must equal the sidecar's own <name> file stem and name an existing agents/<name>.md -- both cross-file checks the companion scanner owns.

spec.description: Only executionRequirements in this slice; SkillMetadata's other spec blocks (portability, lifecycle, references, ...) are deliberately not carried over.

executionRequirements.description: Two recognized categories (tools, lifecycle). filesystem/network/mcp/credentials/browser/externalServices/context are deferred; until they land, any other key is an unknown key and fails closed.

executionRequirementsTools.description: read/write/shell are allow-lists with the same meaning as in SkillMetadata. shellDenylist is a separate deny-list of shell capability tags the agent must never use; it is additive and never changes what shell means.

toolTagList.description: Free-form capability tags, no fixed vocabulary. An explicit empty list states 'none', distinct from the key being absent.

exitCondition.description: A check the agent must pass before it may stop.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within one sidecar (checked by the companion scanner).

command.description: The check to run. Data only: this schema never runs it.

required.description: Whether the condition is a hard gate.

onUnsupported.description: What an adapter must do when it cannot enforce this condition on its runtime. Only fail-closed is accepted in this slice, encoding #307's Layer 3 rule that a hard requirement is never silently downgraded to prompt guidance.
